title: Stewardship and Process Handbook: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel
author: Priya Menon
body:
Purpose

This handbook consolidates company-wide operational policies for access & permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel, and the standard internal templates staff should use. It is intended to be the single source of truth for day-to-day governance and operational decision making. Teams must follow the rules below; exceptions require documented approval from the relevant owner_team and Finance or Legal depending on scope.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all full-time staff, contractors, and vendors with access to Redwood systems and data.
- Covers hosted and private deployments of the platform where Redwood personnel maintain or access customer data.
- Does not replace role-specific security guides (e.g., SRE runbooks) but provides the governance layer those guides must adhere to.

Owners and escalation

- Policy steward: finance-legal (primary)
- Access operations: eng-platform (day-to-day)
- Data classification & retention: security-and-compliance
- Procurement & expense approvals: finance-legal
- Vendor risk & onboarding: security-and-compliance + procurement
- Travel approvals & reimbursement: people-ops + finance-legal

Contact: policy-steward@redwood.ai (for questions, exceptions, and proposed updates)

1) Access & Permissions

Principles
- Least privilege by default: users receive minimal permissions required to perform job functions.
- Role-based assignments: prefer role groups over granting individual permissions.
- Timebound access: elevated access must be issued for a limited time with automated expiry.
- Auditability: all privilege changes must include a reason and ticket reference.

Role matrix (summary)

| Role | Typical groups | Examples of granted capabilities | Approval required |
|------|----------------|----------------------------------|------------------|
| Developer | dev-team-* | Deploy to dev clusters, view CI logs | Team lead approval via PR ticket |
| Infra Engineer | infra-admin | Provision resources, modify infra IaC | Infra manager + change advisory board (CAB) for production changes |
| Support Engineer | support-read | Read production metrics, create support tickets | Support manager |
| IAM Admin | iam-admin | Create groups, change RBAC, revoke keys | Security manager + CFO for org-wide role changes |

Access request and review process
1. Submit request in internal access portal (link: /confluence/tools/access-portal). Include justification, scope, and target duration.
2. Reviewer (team owner) validates least-privilege and suggests narrower role if possible.
3. For production privileges, require secondary approval from eng-sre or infra manager.
4. Automated logging: requests and approvals are stored in audit logs retained per data retention policy.

Temporary privileged access (jump-role)
- Max duration: 8 hours by default; extensions up to 7 days require CAB approval.
- All sessions recorded and traced (session IDs linked to ticket numbers).

Periodic access review
- Quarterly access review mandated for all accounts with production privileges. Team leads must certify or revoke access.

Emergency access exceptions
- Use emergency-access flow (page: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/emergency-access). Emergency approvals must be logged within 24 hours and audited during the next quarterly review.

2) Change Management

Change categories and thresholds
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-authorized changes (e.g., routine config tweaks) — no CAB required but must be recorded.
- Minor change: changes impacting non-production environments or limited scope — team approval required.
- Major change: changes affecting production service availability, data schema, or normal traffic patterns — CAB approval required.
- Emergency change: unplanned, needed to restore availability or prevent data loss — follow emergency playbook and post-facto CAB review.

Change submission checklist (minimum fields)
- Change title and owner
- Business justification
- Risk assessment (impact, rollback plan, validation test plan)
- Scheduled windows and affected services
- Monitoring and alerting hooks to validate success

Rollout patterns and guardrails
- Canary (10% traffic) -> Gradual ramping -> Full rollout; monitor error rates, latency, and user-facing metrics.
- Auto-rollback: if error rate > 3x baseline or p50 latency increases by > 30% for 5 consecutive minutes, rollback trigger is automatic.

Change Advisory Board (CAB) composition
- Chair: eng-platform manager
- Members: infra lead, eng-sre oncall, product owner for affected service, security representative, finance rep when cost-impacting.

Emergency change postmortem
- Every emergency change requires a blameless postmortem within 5 business days that documents root cause, timeline, remediation, and action items.

3) Data classification and management

Classification levels
- PUBLIC: information safe to share externally. No access controls required.
- INTERNAL: organizational information not customer-sensitive. Default for docs and non-prod telemetry.
- SENSITIVE: customer PII, credentials, or business-critical info. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, access controls and audit logging.
- RESTRICTED: regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, PCI) or legal holds. Access only under strict justification and often only within Private deployments.

Handling rules (by classification)
- Storage: SENSITIVE & RESTRICTED must be in approved encrypted stores (KMS-backed).
- Transmission: Use TLS 1.2+; internal messaging channels must be configured to disallow logging of SENSITIVE payloads.
- Retention: Retention windows are applied per-data-scope; default retention for telemetry is 90 days, for SENSITIVE records follow retention defined in data-retention map.
- Deletion: Data deletion requests (user/customer) follow the Data Subject Request flow documented on /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-subject-requests.

Data access approvals and operations
- Data access requests specify dataset, query intent, and duration. Security and data steward must approve for SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED.
- Analysts granted access use ephemeral credentials and are required to operate within an approved secure notebook environment.

Data sharing with third parties
- Contracts must include data processing addenda. Pre-shared risk assessment required for any SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED data exchange.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approval matrix
- <= $2,000: Team lead approval.
- $2,001–$25,000: Department head + finance review.
- > $25,000: VP approval + finance + legal review; multi-year contracts follow legal contracting timelines.
- Recurring SaaS subscriptions require an annual budget line and 30 days notice for cancellation.

Purchasing flow (recommended)
1. Raise PR (purchase request) in procurement system with vendor, SOW, cost center, and justification.
2. Finance reviewer validates budget & cost-center mapping.
3. Legal reviews contract terms (if > $5,000 or involves data handling).
4. Procurement issues PO and tracks delivery.

Expense reimbursement policy
- Use the corporate card where possible. For personal reimbursements: submit within 30 days with receipts.
- Per diem and allowed categories: meals (up to $75/day in high-cost regions), ground transport, lodging (reasonable rate cap defined by country table). Unapproved categories (e.g., personal entertainment) will be declined.

Budget cadence and recordkeeping
- Department budgets set quarterly. Procurement must tag POs with budget codes. All invoices stored in the finance system with a 7-year retention.

5) Vendor management and onboarding

Onboarding checklist
- Business justification and product fit signoff.
- Security questionnaire completion (standard vendor security questionnaire in the procurement portal).
- Legal review of contracts and DPAs for vendors handling data.
- Procurement PO and finance coding.
- Technical integration plan and rollback strategy.

Risk tiers and controls
- Low-risk vendor: SaaS with no data access (e.g., marketing tools) — standard contract and quarterly review.
- Medium-risk vendor: vendors with access to non-sensitive data or administrative access — require security questionnaire, periodic scanning or attestations.
- High-risk vendor: any vendor that stores/processes SENSITIVE/RESTRICTED data or runs infrastructure — must pass security review, provide SOC2/ISO evidence (or equivalent), and may be subject to on-site or in-depth assessment.

Offboarding and termination
- Termination checklist: revoke credentials, remove network access, collect assets, and verify data wipe or return per contractual terms. Procurement and security jointly confirm offboarding completion.

Vendor performance and cost review
- Quarterly review for strategic vendors; yearly review for tactical vendors. Cost variances > 15% require finance and procurement review.

6) Travel policy (business travel and remote work allowances)

Travel approval and booking
- All travel must be pre-approved in the travel portal with estimated costs and business justification. For trips > $5,000 total, VP sign-off required.
- Preferred suppliers and corporate rates should be used where available. No personal upgrades unless pre-approved and self-paid.

Expense submission and allowable items
- Submit receipts within 14 days of trip completion. Use the expense portal and attach digital receipts.
- Allowable: airfare economy or business if flight > 8 hours and pre-approved; hotel at corporate rate; meals up to per diem; ground transport.
- Non-reimbursable: alcohol beyond reasonable meals, personal leisure costs, family expenses.

Travel safety and emergency support
- Register travel through people-ops travel tool for safety alerts. For emergencies, contact travel-support@redwood.ai and oncall HR.

7) Templates and forms (standardized artifacts)

- Access request template: include who, why, scope, duration, and audit ticket ID.
- Change request template: title, owner, impact matrix, rollback plan, test plan, schedule.
- Vendor security questionnaire: standard 60+ item checklist (available in procurement portal).
- Travel pre-approval form: itinerary, budget, meeting attendees, expected outcomes.
- Procurement PR template: vendor, cost center, justification, contract term, renewal date.

(Links to template library: /confluence/policies-and-process/templates)

8) Compliance, audits, and reporting

- Audit schedule: annual internal audit, SOC2 readiness checks twice per year.
- Record retention: key procurement documentation and contracts retained 7 years; access logs and change histories retained 3 years unless tied to sensitive data where retention follows data-retention rules.
- Reporting: monthly governance dashboard showing open access requests, pending changes, procurement pipeline, and top vendor exposures.

9) Exceptions and policy changes

- Exceptions: must be requested via the policy-exceptions form (link: /confluence/policies-and-process/exceptions), include business rationale, compensating controls, and an expiry date. Exceptions require owner_team signoff and a senior exec sponsor if > 90 days.
- Policy review cadence: this handbook is reviewed annually by finance-legal, with operational inputs from eng-platform and security.

Appendices

A. Quick CLI examples
- Revoke AWS IAM session (example):
  aws sts revoke-session --session-id <id> --profile infra-admin  # placeholder example

B. Example change validation checklist (post-rollout)
- Health: p99 latency within 2x baseline
- Errors: SLO error budget consumption unchanged
- User metrics: no negative trend for 24 hours

C. Glossary (short)
- CAB: Change Advisory Board
- DPA: Data Processing Addendum
- PR: Purchase Request

Document history
- 2024-11-15: Created by Priya Menon (finance-legal)
- 2025-01-07: Added vendor risk tiers and procurement thresholds (reviewers: Liam O'Connor, Sara Kim)
- 2025-03-10: Updated retention and emergency access windows after security review

End of handbook

For updates or to propose new templates, contact policy-steward@redwood.ai or open an issue in the policy repo.
